analysis.requirement: R7 — Global uncertainty and sensitivity analysis: propagate joint uncertainty in population locations/counts, network completeness, walking speed/mobility, behavioral coefficients, facility capacity/availability, outreach reach, smoke concentration, indoor filtration, and candidate-site feasibility via Morris screening, LHS, or Sobol indices; test whether the headline awareness-vs-capacity conclusion survives defensible joint ranges.
exists_defensible: Honest scoping of what seed stability proves: the manuscript states the 27-run seed spread (11 residents) and the smallest between-scenario gap (306) 'side by side rather than as a ratio: seed spread bounds only Monte-Carlo variability, not structural or parametric uncertainty' (docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:281, read directly). This framing survives review; it also concedes the R7 gap in-text.

A real one-dimensional capacity sweep with archived runs: BS080-BS160, 7 scale levels x 3 seeds, 21 run directories verified present (docs/runs/phaseD-bed-sweep/BS080..BS160-seed42..44/simulation.json), reported in the tex with two pre-registered predictions scored as MISSES (docs/chapter/Capacity_Is_Not_Access.tex:864-874, read directly; docs/critique-response/12-PHASD-D-PREDICTIONS per evidence inventory). This is genuine 1-D sensitivity on the most load-bearing parameter, with disclosed disconfirmation.
Triage-reserve 1-D sweep: r00/r10/r15/r25 run directories verified (docs/runs/scenario-d-2026/D-seed42-r00..r25/simulation.json, plus r10/r15 at seeds 43-44).
Observation-window sweep W24/W72 x A/B/C x 3 seeds, 18 run directories verified (docs/runs/phaseD-windows/).

Structural probes that partially address two R7 axes: (a) freeway-removal re-run left all sheltered counts 'unchanged to the digit' (md:281) — one network-completeness perturbation; (b) candidate-site uncertainty probed by 18 archived random-site control runs, 6 draws x 3 seeds (docs/runs/scenario-crandom-2026/CR2026r1-3, CP2026r4-6, verified listing), which demoted the placement attribution to dispersion; (c) three Scenario-E closure draws with a draw-dependent sign flip disclosed as prediction miss P-SE10 (docs/critique-response/13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md per inventory).
Two smoke severities exist as labeled counterfactual scenarios (1.75x and Canberra-anchored 4.436x) — coarse variation of the smoke axis, though framed as scenarios, not uncertainty propagation.

Prior elicitation already done: Geography/data/registry/variables.csv carries a per-variable 'uncertainty' column with defensible ranges (verified rows: V25 IR walking 1.2-2.0 / resting 0.4-0.8 m3/h; V38 alphaHazard +/-1 log-odds; V39 gammaVuln 0-0.5; V40 barrier costs 0.10-0.42; V41 outreach 0-0.2/day). The raw inputs for a global SA design exist on file.

The design intent is on record: docs/science/phase2-human-agents/04-DECISION.md:220-224 (read directly) names 'seven to eight sensitivity dimensions — tractable with a one-at-a-time or fractional-factorial design under common random numbers'.

A two-point bracket on the single most contested parameter exists: legacy arms run awareness=1.0 (declared upper bound, md:289) and Phase-E baseline-real arms run awareness=0.356 (registry V29, Wilson CI 0.25-0.47), both archived in docs/runs/.
missing: ABSENT: any global or joint SA method. Repo-wide grep for Sobol/Morris/Latin hypercube/Saltelli/variance-based/elementary effects returns zero methodological hits (only Morrison Bridge and a package-lock hash); the enumerated docs/runs/ families are all one-factor (arms x seeds, bed scale, window, site draw, reserve fraction, closure draw, smoke series). No joint-variation run family exists.

The two arms on record answer it oppositely — under universal awareness, capacity/placement binds (30.1/91.6/96.0%); under awareness 0.356, awareness binds (17.8% sheltered per P-E1 scoring) — and no analysis connects them across joint ranges. No headline number carries a propagated uncertainty interval; only seed ranges (~11 residents) are reported.
implementable_with_existing_data: Morris screening / LHS over the registry's own ranges — no new data needed, only runs: use Geography/data/registry/variables.csv 'uncertainty' column (verified ranges for IR, hazard coefficients, barrier costs, outreach, choice weights, speed cells) plus assumptions.csv sweep plans (A-04, A-09) as the design space; drive via the existing Repast batch machinery and check with scripts/verify_2026_runs.py-style invariants.

Population-location bootstrap: resample the 3,400 report rows of Geography/data/encampments/irp_campsite_reports_sample.csv (inc_date column verified present, spanning 2025-01..2026-07) — spatial block bootstrap plus temporal-window splits, supporting a location-uncertainty replicate axis; is_vehicle (1,283/2,117) supports a subpopulation-sensitivity split.

Capacity-conversion Monte Carlo: sample per-facility unit-conversion factors from the documented ranges instead of midpoints, using Geography/data/shelters/shelters_multnomah_2026.csv (capacity_unit column) and the bracket arithmetic in docs/final/SHELTER_CAPACITY_AUDIT.md:56-98 (~1,885-2,224 people county-wide); propagates the capacity axis the knife-edge sweep showed is decisive.
A-04 historical capacity sweep: vary the 99-per-site values in Geography/data/shelters/shelters_2020-09.csv against the ~130 observation — the registry's own stated but unexecuted plan.

Smoke uncertainty from the existing AQS file: single-monitor vs two-monitor-mean bracketing and a multiplicative bias factor from Geography/data/airnow/aqs_hourly_pm25_portland_2020-09.csv (1,454 Multnomah rows); plus simply running the already-registered smokeScale 0.857/1.143 arms.

Ventilation-rate re-sweep 0.25-0.80 m3/h per D16's own recommendation (registry V25 row); the exported airVolumeBreathedM3 decomposition in archived agents.csv plausibly allows partial post-hoc recomputation of dose sensitivity without re-running (decomposition claim REPORTED from the model inventory).

Network-completeness perturbation: random edge-dropout and street-class removal experiments on the existing RLIS graph (Geography/data/Streets.*), extending the executed freeway-removal precedent and the specified-but-deferred TYPE-1200 test.

The central-question factorial: pAwareInit over its Wilson CI 0.25-0.47 (registry V29) crossed with capacity scale 0.8-1.6x reusing the existing BS-sweep configuration — directly answers whether awareness dominates capacity across defensible joint ranges.

Demographic-marginal resampling: binomial/Wilson draws on the survey fractions already documented with numerators and denominators (awareness 26/73, attempt 10/26, mobility 391/2037, dependents 30/6831) inside the LHS design — all counts in the registry and DATA_SOURCES.
needs_new_empirical_data: Indoor filtration effectiveness: no indoor PM2.5 data or filtration model exists anywhere in the repo (deliberately out of scope, endpoint = arrival at door); would need paired indoor/outdoor low-cost PM2.5 sensors at operating shelters during a smoke event, or on-site HVAC/filtration audits, before this R7 axis can even enter the model.

Locally valid behavioral coefficients: the repo records that no fitted quantitative shelter-choice model for unsheltered people exists in any literature it found; closing this needs a stated-preference / discrete-choice survey of unsheltered Portland residents (departure triggers, barrier trade-offs, destination choice).
Walking speeds of unsheltered residents: md:303 states no local validation was possible; would need a consented field gait-speed measurement protocol in partnership with service providers.

Outreach reach: registry V41 states 'a real outreach-contact rate for this event does not exist in the record'; would need prospective outreach-contact logging (contacts/day per team, conversion to awareness) with the county's 27 outreach partners.
needs_external_acquisition: Primary JOHS/Multnomah County 2020 after-action documentation of clean-air shelter capacity and nightly occupancy (candidate source: county public-records request to the Joint Office of Homeless Services) — would replace the blocking newsroom-sourced A-04 anchor with a documented value or range and add calibration points for the historical arm.

PurpleAir low-cost sensor archive for Portland, Sept 2020 (candidate source: PurpleAir historical data API) — dozens of intra-urban sensors would empirically bound the error of the county-uniform smoke assumption; availability and QC for 2020 not checked from this repo.
Modeled smoke surfaces for Sept 2020 (candidate sources: NOAA HRRR-Smoke archive; EPA fused CMAQ/downscaler daily PM2.5 surfaces) — alternative spatial fields for a structural smoke-uncertainty axis.

A dated RLIS street-centerline release contemporaneous with 2020 (candidate source: Oregon Metro RLIS archive/discovery site) — the current file's vintage is unknown (Geography/data/README.md per inventory); a dated release would bound network-vintage uncertainty.

Shelter occupancy time series for the present-day system (candidate source: JOHS data request; the repo notes the county Tableau dashboard was not machine-readable) — would let capacity-availability uncertainty be calibrated rather than assumed.

PIT-count uncertainty documentation (candidate sources: HUD PIT methodology notes, Multnomah County PIT reports) — defensible priors for the unsheltered-count axis (6,842 vs 6,731 service count is currently the only bracket in the repo).

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: 'C's siting advantage on headcount is bounded at about 342 spaces' / 'worth at most about 342 spaces'
claims_exceeding_evidence.location: docs/chapter/Capacity_Is_Not_Access.tex:873 and tex:1066 (also tex:73, tex:738; read directly at 864-874)
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: An 'at most' universal bound derived from a one-dimensional capacity sweep at 3 seeds with every other uncertain input fixed at its point value (midpoint capacity conversions, universal awareness, one campsite draw, fixed speed distributions). Under joint uncertainty the bound is conditional; nothing in the repo tests whether 342 survives varying any second parameter.

No IR-sweep run family exists in the enumerated docs/runs/ archives, and the registry's own V25 row (read directly) states the declared resting range 0.4-0.8 excludes the EPA source's own Sedentary/Passive cells (0.252-0.300) — so the sweep is both unexecuted-in-archives and, as specified, too narrow to cover the defensible range.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: Registry uncertainty column uses past tense 'swept' for behavioral coefficients (e.g., 'each barrier cost swept 0.10-0.42 log-odds', 'swept 0-0.2 per day', 'swept 0 to +0.5')
claims_exceeding_evidence.location: Geography/data/registry/variables.csv rows V38-V41 (read directly); same pattern in V35-V37, V43 per inventory
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: These rows carry status 'specified', no run archive sweeps any of these coefficients, and 13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:256 confirms even the registered smokeScale sweep never ran. Past-tense wording reads as executed coverage that does not exist; a reviewer auditing the registry against docs/runs/ will find the discrepancy.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: 'The present 36-facility system shelters 30.1% of residents' (and the 91.6%/96.0%/550/244 headline figures generally)
claims_exceeding_evidence.location: docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:27, md:315 (per inventory; robustness context read directly at md:281)
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Three-significant-figure point estimates whose only quantified interval is a seed range of ~11 residents, while known input uncertainties (capacity unit conversions spanning tens of percent, awareness CI 0.25-0.47, unconfirmed A-04, population count/location, 0.61 IR defect) are disclosed but never propagated into any interval. Relative to R7 the precision exceeds the propagated evidence.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: 'at 1.1x (684 spaces) every reachable resident is admitted and the gap vanishes' — sharp knife-edge thresholds
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: The 1.05x/1.1x thresholds come from a 5%-grid sweep of a capacity inventory whose own unit-conversion uncertainty exceeds the grid spacing; the threshold is also stated as 1.2x in two results docs (README_RESULTS.md:228-230 per inventory), so the sharp value is neither propagated nor internally consistent across deliverables.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: The mobility-limited worst-served finding 'survives every measure'
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Robustness is demonstrated only across reporting scales (pp gap / ratio / headcount) and 9 seeds — never across parametric or structural uncertainty. The phrase invites a stronger robustness reading than the evidence supports; the finding is also conditioned on FCFS admission and the unswept Boyce speed distribution.

proposed_methods: Stage 1 — Morris elementary-effects screening: r = 20-40 trajectories over k ~ 15-25 parameters, with ranges lifted directly from the variables.csv uncertainty column plus documented brackets (capacity conversion factors, capacity scale, 2020 capacity 60-140, awareness 0.25-0.47, outreach 0-0.2/day, alphaHazard +/-1, bRisk 0.25-0.55, wOfficial 0.6-1.7, gammaVuln 0-0.5, sigmaTheta 0.5-1.5, betaS 0-0.5, barrier costs 0.10-0.42, speed-cell means +/- published SEs, CV 0.10-0.16, Boyce mu/sigma, COPD delta CI, IR walking 1.2-2.0 / resting 0.25-0.80, departure threshold 35.5-150.5, smoke bias 0.8-1.3, pet-policy default, belongings 0.108-0.46). ~(k+1) x r = 400-1,000 runs — the project has already executed 84+ run matrices, and the byte-parity websim TypeScript engine (Tier 0-4 fidelity ladder, REPORTED) could serve as the fast engine with per-design-point spot parity checks against the Java model.

Stage 2 — variance decomposition on the 6-10 surviving parameters: Sobol first-order and total indices via Saltelli sampling, on the headline outputs (sheltered %, refusals, mobility gap on all three scales, inhaled dose, and the B-vs-C ordering indicator). If the run budget binds, LHS n = 500-1,000 with PRCC plus a Gaussian-process emulator; use common random numbers per the project's own design note (04-DECISION.md:223-224).

Structural axes crossed as discrete scenario dimensions inside the design: campsite bootstrap replicate (spatial block bootstrap of irp_campsite_reports_sample.csv), network edge-dropout replicate (extending the freeway-removal precedent), closure draw r1-r3, admission rule (FCFS vs order-independent two-phase, simultaneously resolving A-16), pet-policy default, and smoke-field variant (uniform vs single-monitor brackets).

Central-question test: a dedicated awareness x capacity-scale factorial (or the Sobol interaction index for that pair) answering whether 'awareness dominates capacity' across the joint range — currently answered oppositely by the two disconnected arm families.

Conclusion-stability reporting (scenario-discovery/PRIM style): for each headline qualitative claim (placement's headcount contribution is dispersion; surplus dissolves the equity gap; mobility-limited are worst-served; awareness binds before capacity), report the fraction of joint-uncertainty draws in which it holds, and the parameter regions where it fails.

Uncertainty-aware headline reporting: replace seed ranges with propagated intervals (e.g., 30.1% -> a joint-uncertainty interval) in abstract and summary sentences; resample survey-derived marginals (26/73, 10/26, 391/2037) as binomial draws inside the design rather than fixing them.

Bookkeeping to prevent recurrence of the 'swept'-wording defect: add an executed-sweep column (run-family id) to variables.csv so declared ranges and executed coverage cannot be conflated, and extend lint_claims.py with a rule that flags 'swept'/'sensitivity-swept' claims lacking a run-archive reference.
analysis.priority_rationale: This is among the most load-bearing unmet requirements for this project, and the repo itself concedes it: the manuscript states in its own robustness section that seed spread 'bounds only Monte-Carlo variability, not structural or parametric uncertainty' (md:281, read directly) — the R7 gap is admitted in-text without being closed. Three verified facts make it acute rather than pro forma. First, the project's own 1-D sweep found a knife edge: +5% capacity reproduces C's headline admissions and +10% dissolves the equity gap (tex:864-874, read directly), while the capacity input itself carries unit-conversion uncertainty at least that large plus an unconfirmed newsroom-sourced 99-bed anchor (A-04, registry-flagged blocking) — so the paper's headline orderings and its '342 spaces' bound sit inside plausible input error, and only a joint analysis can show whether they survive. Second, the central awareness-vs-capacity question is currently answered both ways by two disconnected arm families (universal awareness: capacity/placement binds at 30.1/91.6/96.0%; awareness 0.356: awareness binds at ~17.8% sheltered), with no analysis connecting them. Third, absence is a choice, not a constraint: the per-parameter ranges are already elicited in variables.csv, the batch and verification machinery exists, a fast byte-parity TS engine exists, and the project's own science tier proposed the design (04-DECISION.md:223) — a reviewer at IJGIS/ERL will see all of this in the repo and will not accept 'deferred'. What depends on it: every headline number in the abstract, the 342-space siting bound, the knife-edge thresholds, the equity-gap trajectory, and the paper's core claim that its comparisons (not just its absolutes) are robust. Two registry/report wording defects found here ('swept' past tense for unexecuted sweeps; 'sensitivity-swept' ventilation) should be fixed regardless, since they overstate exactly the coverage this requirement demands.
